label: def:dosp
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:dosp}
	Let $(S_1, \dots, S_p)$ be an ordered set partition of $ [n] $ and $(s_1, \dots, s_p)$ be a composition of $k$.
	There is an equivalence relation on these pairs, defined by
	\[
		((S_1)_{s_1},(S_2)_{s_2},\dots,(S_p)_{s_p}) \sim
		((S_2)_{s_2},\dots,(S_p)_{s_p},(S_1)_{s_1}).
	\]
	A \emph{decorated ordered set partition}
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:dosp}
		\mathsf{S} = [((S_1)_{s_1},\dots,(S_p)_{s_p})]
	\end{equation}
	is an equivalence class of such pairs.
	A decorated ordered set partition is \emph{hypersimplicial} if $ 1 \leq s_i \leq |S_i|-1 $ for all $ i $. We denote the set of hypersimplicial decorated
	ordered set partitions of type $ (k,n) $ by $ \operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n) $. We call each $ S_i $ a block, place the blocks on a
	circle clockwise, and regard $ s_i $ as the clockwise distance between adjacent blocks $ S_i $ and $ S_{i+1} $. The
	\emph{winding number} of $ \mathsf{S} $ is defined as the number of times we wrap around the circle as we trace $ 1 \to
		2 \to \cdots \to n \to 1 $ clockwise.
head: environment

title: Remark
head: environment

label: thm:earlykim
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:earlykim}
	The $ h^* $ -polynomial of the hypersimplex $ \Delta_{k,n} $ is given by
	\[
		h^*(\Delta_{k,n},z) = \sum_{\mathsf{S} \in \operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n)} z^{\operatorname{wind}(\mathsf{S})}.
	\]
head: environment

label: ex:d24
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:d24}
	The hypersimplex $ \Delta_{2,4} $
	is the octahedron shown in Figure~\ref{fig:d24}.
	The hypersimplicial decorated ordered set partitions of type $ (2,4) $
	are shown in Figure~\ref{fig:dosp24}, and we have
	\[
		h^*(\Delta_{2,4},z) = 1 + 2z + z^2.
	\]

label: def:balanced
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:balanced}
	A \emph{balanced complex} of type $ (a_1,\dots,a_m) $ is a pair $ (\Delta,\pi) $ such that $ \Delta $ is a pure $ \delta $
	-complex on a vertex set $ V $ and $\pi=(V_1,\ldots, V_m)$ is an ordered set partition of $ V $
	such that for every maximal face $ F\in\Delta $ and every $ i\in[m] $, we have $ |F\cap V_i|=a_i $. Hence $
		a_1+\cdots+a_m=\delta+1 $.
	A balanced complex of type $ (1,1,\dots,1) $
	is \emph{completely balanced}.

title: Definition
body_md:
For each subset $ S \subseteq [n] $ and for each $i \in S$, we associate a cyclic composition, denoted
	$\operatorname{comp}^{(i)}(S)$. We draw the points in $S$ clockwise on a circle, so that they cut the circle into $ |S| $ arcs. Let
	$\operatorname{comp}^{(i)}(S)_j$ be the arc length of the $j$-th arc clockwise after $i$. These arc lengths form a cyclic composition
	of $n$. The set $\{\operatorname{comp}^{(i)}(S): i \in S\}$ forms an equivalence class of compositions, which we denote by $\operatorname{ccomp}(S)$.
	Conventionally, let $\operatorname{comp}(S):= \operatorname{comp}^{\min S}(S)$.

label: def:hypersimplicial
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:hypersimplicial}
	Let $\alpha$ be a weak composition with $k$ parts.
	Viewing $\alpha: \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, we say that $\alpha \models n$ is \emph{hypersimplicial} if every positive entry satisfies $ \alpha_i > 1 $ and is
	followed by at most $ \alpha_i - 1 $ zeros on the circle.
	A cyclic word is \emph{hypersimplicial} if it has
	hypersimplicial content.

body_md:
A sequence $ (I_1,\dots,I_n) $ of $ k $ -subsets of $ [n] $
	is a \emph{circuit} if for each $ i \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} $, there exists $ j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} $ such that $
		I_{i+1} = I_i \setminus \{j\} \cup \{j+1\} $.

label: thm:coloring
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:coloring}
	The alcove triangulation complex $ \mathcal{T}_{k,n} $ of $ \Delta_{k,n} $
	is completely balanced with respect to the coloring $
		\operatorname{color}(I):\equiv \sum_{i \in I} i \bmod n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $F$ is a maximal face with circuits $(I_0,\dots,I_{n-1})$, then \[\operatorname{color}(I_{p}) \equiv \operatorname{color}(I_{p-1}) + 1 \bmod n, \qquad \text{ for any }p \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}, \] so all the vertices of $F$ are of different colors, and each color appears only once. Any lower dimensional face is
    contained in a maximal face, and this property is inherited.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: Let $d = \gcd(k,n)$. For every $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, the flag numbers satisfy $f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = f_{S+k}(\mathcal{T}_{k,n})$ and $h_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = h_{S+k}(\mathcal{T}_{k,n})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the rotation of the $n$-coordinates
	\[
		\rho: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n, (x_1,\dots,x_n) \mapsto
		(x_2,\dots,x_{n},x_1)
	\]
	which preserves the alcove triangulation. Then $\operatorname{type}(\rho F) = \operatorname{type}(F) + k$ and $f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = f_{S+k}(\mathcal{T}_{k,n})$.
	Applying M\"obius transformation, we obtain the same equality for $h_S$.

label: lem:alcove_to_word
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item\label{item1}
		Suppose that $ F=(I_0,\dots,I_{n-1}) $
		is a maximal face, and $w$ is a permutation taken from Theorem~\ref{thm:max_face} with $w(n)=1$.
		By~\eqref{eq:circuit}, we see that $I_p$ is lexicographically greater than $I_{p-1}$ for $p \geq 1$.
		If $ F $ is a face of lower dimension, then we may embed it into a maximal face, and the conclusion follows from the case for maximal faces.
		\item For a maximal face $ F $ with $ w \in S_n $ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:max_face}, we have $ A_i =
		\{w^{-1}(i)\} $. They are mutually disjoint because $ w $ is a permutation. For lower dimensional faces, we
		embed them into maximal faces to conclude.
		\item Suppose that $ F $ is a maximal face, and $ w \in S_n $ is as in Theorem~\ref{thm:max_face}. Moreover,
		by~(\ref{item1}), we may assume that $ w(n) = 1 $. Then $ w_F = w $ and $ \operatorname{base}(F) = \operatorname{cDes}(w) $
		by~\eqref{eq:cDescirc}. If $ F $ is lower dimensional, we may embed $ F $ into a maximal face $ F' $ with a
		permutation $ w $ with $ w(n) = 1 $ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:max_face} and~(\ref{item1}). Consequently, $
		\operatorname{base}(F') = \operatorname{cDes}(w) $. As $ F \subseteq F' $, the tuple $ (A_1,\dots,A_p) $ is an ordered set partition of
		which $ w $ is a refinement, and $ w_F $ is the reading word~\eqref{eq:reading-osp} of $ (A_1,\dots,A_p) $. The
		set $ \operatorname{cDes}(w_F) $ consists of indices $ i $ that appear in a later block than $ i+1 $, and the set $ \operatorname{cEq}(w_F)
		$ consists of indices $ i $ that appear in the same block as $ i+1 $. As $ w $ is a refinement of $
		(A_1,\dots,A_p) $, the conclusion follows. Conversely, given the word $ w: \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, let $A_i$ be the
		preimage of $i$ under $w$. We can form $ (I_1,\dots,I_p) $ inductively by setting $ I_1 $ to $ I $, and use $
		I_p = I_{p-1}+\alpha_{A_i} $.
		\item We may assume that $ \operatorname{cdes}(w) \leq k $. The condition on $ I $ means that $ I \setminus \operatorname{cDes}(w) $ can be
		any subset of $ \operatorname{cEq}(w) $ with cardinality $ k-\operatorname{cdes}(w) $, hence the conclusion.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
Choose $F = (I_0,I_1)$ such that $I_0 = \{1,2\}, I_1 = \{2,4\}$, and embed $F$ into the face in Example~\ref{ex:maxface}.
	We have $I_1 - I_0 = (e_3-e_2) + (e_4-e_3) = \alpha_3 + \alpha_4$ so $A_1 = \{3,4\}$ and $A_2 = \{1,2\}$.
	The reading word of this ordered set partition is $w_F = 2211$.
	We have $\operatorname{cDes}(w_F) = \{2\}$ and $\operatorname{cEq}(w_F) = \{1,3\}$.

label: prop:compF
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $ F \in \mathcal{T}_{k,n} $ and $ w_F $
	be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:alcove_to_word}. By~(\ref{item1}), $
		\operatorname{color}(I_{i+1}) = \operatorname{color}(I_i) + |A_i| $. Therefore, $
		\alpha(\operatorname{type}(F)^{\operatorname{color}(\operatorname{base}(F))}) = (|A_1|,\dots,|A_p|) $. By~\eqref{eq:wF}, $ w_F $
	is the reading word of $ (A_1,\dots,A_p) $, so $
		\operatorname{content}(w_F) = \alpha(\operatorname{type}(F)^{\operatorname{color}(\operatorname{base}(F))}) $. The definition of $ \operatorname{base}(F) $ forces $ w_F(n) = p $. For each such word $w$, Lemma~\ref{lem:alcove_to_word} (4) shows that there are $\binom{\operatorname{ceq}(w)}{k - \operatorname{cdes}(w)}$ possible choices of $\operatorname{base}(F)$.
head: environment

title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Summing over all $\operatorname{comp}(F) = \beta \in [\alpha]$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:compF}, we obtain the desired equality.
head: environment

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $ F $ be a face with $ \operatorname{type}(F) = S $, and let $ w_F $
	be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:alcove_to_word}. Since $ \operatorname{type}(F) = S $, there exists $ i \in S $ such that $ \operatorname{color}(\operatorname{base}(F)) = i $.
	By Lemma~\ref{lem:alcove_to_word}, $
		\operatorname{cDes}(w_F) \subseteq \operatorname{base}(F) \subseteq \operatorname{cDes}(w_F) \cup \operatorname{cEq}(w_F) $
, so the inner sum is a generating function of $
		q^{\sum_{j \in \operatorname{base}(F)} j} $.

label: eq:nZaction
title: Proof
body_md:
The $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ action on cyclic words generated by
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:nZaction}
		w \mapsto w', \qquad w'(i) = w(i-1),
	\end{equation}
	preserves $\operatorname{cdes}$ and $\operatorname{ceq}$.
	There are $\alpha_1$ many $i$ such that $w(i) = 1$, so the left hand side counts the number of pairs $(w,i)$ for which $w\in W(\alpha)$ and $w(i) = 1$, weighted by the binomial coefficient.
	The right hand side applies the $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ action to $w$ with $w(n) = 1$ and counts the same set of pairs with the same weight.

label: cor:Gsym
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Gsym}
	The sum
	\[
		\sum_{w \in W(\alpha)} \binom{\operatorname{ceq}(w)}{k - \operatorname{cdes}(w)} = \langle h_\alpha, G_{k,n} \rangle
	\]
	depends only on the multiset of parts of $ \alpha $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By definition, $\operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n}$ is a symmetric function. By Theorem~\ref{thm:GHyp}, $G_{k,n}$ is also a symmetric function. The definition of $G_{k,n}$ expands it into the monomial basis $\{m_\alpha\}$ of the ring of symmetric functions. Since the monomial symmetric function is dual to the complete homogeneous symmetric function, taking inner product with $h_\alpha$ extracts the coefficient of $m_\alpha$, which is the left hand side.

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\gcd(k,n) = 1$, by Corollary~\ref{cor:gcd}, the left hand side of Theorem~\ref{thm:ftoG} is equal to $n f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n})$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:GHyp}, the right hand side is equal to $\frac{n}{k} \langle h_\alpha, \operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n} \rangle$.
	The character of $M^\alpha$ is $h_\alpha$, and the character of $\mathcal{M}_{k,n}$ is $\operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n}$, so the dimension of $\operatorname{Hom}_{S_n}(M^\alpha, \mathcal{M}_{k,n})$ is equal to $\langle h_\alpha, \operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n} \rangle$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We construct a bijection between hypersimplicial words $w$ with $\operatorname{cDes}(w) \subseteq S$, content $\lambda$, and contingency tables with row sum $\alpha$ and column sum $\lambda$.
	Let $(a_{ij})$ be such a contingency table, with row sum $\alpha$ and column sum $\lambda$.
	Let $w$ be the word with $a_{11}$ ones followed by $a_{12}$ twos, etc., up to $a_{1n}$ $n$'s, then $a_{21}$ ones, $a_{22}$ twos, etc.
	By construction, $\operatorname{cDes}(w) \subseteq S$ for any $S$ with $\operatorname{comp}(S) = \alpha$ and $\operatorname{content}(w) = \lambda$.

label: eq:mainmobius
title: Proof
body_md:
By M\"obius inversion,
	\[
		f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = \sum_{T \subseteq S} h_T(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}),
	\]
	so it suffices to prove that
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:mainmobius}
		\sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = \sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} \left| \left\{ \mathsf{S} \in \operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n): \operatorname{cDes}(\mathsf{S}) \subseteq S \right\} \right|.
	\end{equation}
	By the bijection from $\operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n) \times \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z} $ onto hypersimplicial words via $(\mathsf{S}, p)\mapsto w_\mathsf{S}^{(p)}$,
	we multiply both sides of~\eqref{eq:mainmobius} by $k$ to obtain
	\begin{equation}
		\begin{aligned}
			k\sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} f_S(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) & = \sum_{p \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}}\sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} \left| \left\{ \mathsf{S} \in \operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n): \operatorname{cDes}(w_\mathsf{S}^{(p)}) \subseteq S \right\} \right| \\
			                                          & = \sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} \left| \left\{ (\mathsf{S},p) \in \operatorname{hDOSP}(k,n) \times \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}: \operatorname{cDes}(w_\mathsf{S}^{(p)}) \subseteq S \right\} \right| \\
			                                          & = \sum_{S: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]} W_S.
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
	Fix some $S \subseteq [n]$ with $\operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]$ and let $O(S) = \{S+j: j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\}$ be the orbit of $S$ under the $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ action, and let $\operatorname{Stab}(S)$ be the stabilizer of $S$ under this action.
	By the orbit-stabilizer theorem,
	\[
		\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} f_{S+j}(\mathcal{T}_{k,n}) = |\operatorname{Stab}(S)| \sum_{S' \in O(S)} f_{S'}.
	\]
	The set $\{S \subseteq [n]: \operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]\}$ is a union of such orbits, so it suffices to show that
	\[
		\sum_{S' \in O(S)} f_{S'} = \sum_{S' \in O(S)} |W_{S'}|.
	\]
	Again by the orbit stabilizer theorem,
	\[
		|\operatorname{Stab}(S)| \sum_{S' \in O(S)} |W_{S'}| = \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} |W_{S+j}|.
	\]
	However, if $\operatorname{ccomp}(S) = [\alpha]$, then $\operatorname{ccomp}(S+j) = [\alpha]$, so the right hand side is equal to $n |W_S| = n
	\langle h_\alpha, \operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n}\rangle$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:contingency}. By Theorem~\ref{thm:ftoG} we reduce the theorem to
	\[
		k \langle h_\alpha, G_{k,n} \rangle = n \langle h_\alpha, \operatorname{Hyp}_{k,n} \rangle
	\]
	which holds by Theorem~\ref{thm:GHyp}.
